correctness.rationale: The nonzero-gauge transform is derived from the Fourier transform of the odd Gaussian. Exclusive real/imaginary factors reduce all zeros to the two time slices. Strict monotonicity of \(\operatorname{artanh}(u)/u\) and a strictly decreasing exterior logarithmic function yield exactly one positive interior root iff gap exceeds \(\sqrt{2/\pi}\), and exactly one positive exterior root always; reflection gives completeness. Jacobian signs follow from explicit derivative formulas and monotone crossing; at equality \(F^{(3)}(0)=8\pi e^{-1/2}\) and nonzero imaginary time derivative establish the cubic-contact local degree. The actual embedded verify.py was run and gave VERIFY_OK with 94 checks, including independent direct quadrature. Finite checks supplement, not replace, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact gap threshold and complete three-to-five zero/charge bifurcation resolve a natural deterministic analogue of the newly studied signed-zero geometry for Hermite spectrograms. Unlike a bare two-tone formula, the finding certifies that there are no hidden frequency zeros, locates persistent exterior defects, proves local orientation transfers and the cubic critical contact, and yields a sharp square-root splitting law. This is a structural phase diagram for the lowest non-Gaussian Hermite window, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
